title: Resolve and validate the isolated development-tooling dependency baseline
summary: Resolved the three orchestrator tooling runtime dependencies (pydantic, cryptography, packaging) and their full transitive closure against official PyPI latest stable releases under Python 3.12.3. Established the isolated tooling lockfile at dependencies/locks/orchestrator.txt, documented the reference in .orchestrator/requirements.txt, and validated the isolated environment through preflight checks, full tooling import contract tests, task-state-store tests, ai-status CLI tests, and dev-bridge Ed25519-signed packet intake. Kept dependency closure strictly separate from product/ML runtime, with zero mutation to live supervisor config, account grouping, quota, leases, credentials, installed CLIs, or model/slot settings.

not_changing: live supervisor config, account grouping, quota, leases, credentials, installed CLIs, model/slot settings (acceptance criterion 3)
product/BFF or ML/research requirements and runtimes (kept strictly isolated)
supervisor dispatch logic, watchdog, or auto-integrator

review_decision.note: Independently verify against this exact head: (1) .orchestrator/requirements.txt preserves the minimal supervisor dependency contract (pydantic>=2.9,<3, cryptography>=42,<51, packaging>=23,<27) and references the lockfile; (2) dependencies/locks/orchestrator.txt accurately pins all 3 direct dependencies and all 6 transitive dependencies to official latest stable non-yanked versions under Python 3.12; (3) pip install from dependencies/locks/orchestrator.txt succeeds cleanly in an isolated interpreter; (4) validate_python_dependencies preflight probe passes; (5) contract tests for supervisor config, dev-bridge intake, task state store, and ai-status pass; (6) zero mutation to live supervisor config, account grouping, quota, leases, credentials, installed CLIs, or model/slot settings.
